Several drills on the market use soil movement from fluted coulters to improve drill performance over a wide variety of soil conditions. Selection of the coulter type should be determined by operator preference and field conditions. For example, drills operating in heavy residue may need to be pulled at a slight angle to the old corn row to get the corn residue to feed through. Idaho Soil Health Case Study is an NRCS and American Farmland Trust case study that examines the soil health practices (including no-till) implemented by a farm in central Idaho. [...] Soil is a complex system of living and non-living elements. Soil contains a microbial biomass of fungi, bacteria, and fine roots that aggregate (collect) and store nutrients for plants. Conventional tillage breaks up soil aggregates and reduces the soil microbial biomass. Because no-till farming does not break up soil by plowing or turning it, soil microbial biomass remains undisturbed and intact. In addition, no-till benefits predatory insects that can  enhance pest control. [...] Enhancing Soil Health: No-till systems enrich the soil with organic matter, increase soil water-holding capacity, and protect crops during periods of drought and flooding. requirements.missing: No supplied document addresses both (a) laboratory or field germination parameter values for alfalfa and (b) mechanical/management practices for preventing or breaking soil crust during alfalfa seedling emergence. s11 notes crusted soils impede slow cold-season emergence but does not provide crust-breaking methods; s20 warns against powdery-fine seedbeds that crust but gives no crust-breaking procedure; no source covers germination parameter tables alongside crust-management practices.

No supplied document provides germination temperature values with original units tied to alfalfa seed imbibition or emergence together with soil moisture metrics for the same process, preserving source geography and date. s11 gives 31.3–32.2 °F and 60 °F with UMN Extension (April 2022, Minnesota) but no soil-moisture metric; s10 cites 81 °F air / 54 °F soil for optimal growth, not germination imbibition; s14 reports water-potential thresholds in MPa from Lanzhou University (2022) but no germination temperature values; s13 reports germination decline under PEG-induced drought without temperature-imbibition linkage.
